I will keep my land mainly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 7.8 mu and it fits my experience, labor, and irrigation conditions. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will not make the management too complicated or too risky. I will put 6.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 1.8 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for a stable stand, add phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate at key stages, and keep rotary tillage because it is practical on my small farm. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on that same 6.0 mu, use no-tillage to save time and labor, and rely on a couple of irrigations and basic pest control to protect yield. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more labor and more spraying, but I will still grow it since it helps spread risk and gives me another source of income. Overall, I will manage for steady output, lower labor pressure, and dependable production with the well water I already have.
